title: Cross-Region Call Safety: Standardize Retry Windows, Idempotency Contracts, and Hedged-Request Patterns
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Different services and SDKs currently implement divergent retry windows, timeout semantics, and hedged-request behavior. During cross-region failovers and heavy load events this leads to duplicate side-effects, inconsistent user-facing latencies, and uneven load shedding. Goal: Define a single, pragmatic standard for retry windows (client and server), idempotency key handling, hedged request timing, and safe defaults for load shedding and circuit breakers that can be adopted across server services and official SDKs. Scope: API servers, gateway/proxy, SDK clients (JS/Python/Go), and guidance for private/dedicated deployments. Out of scope: legacy third-party clients not maintained by Redwood (we will publish compatibility guidance).
acceptance_criteria: A concise spec exists that defines: client retry window, server deduplication window, idempotency key lifecycle, hedged request timing parameters (initial latency threshold and max parallel hedges), and explicit interaction rules with circuit breakers and load shedding.
All Redwood SDKs implement the client-side defaults from the spec and expose opt-in knobs for advanced users (e.g., override retry window, supply idempotency key, toggle hedging).
Server-side runtime honors idempotency keys and maintains a deduplication TTL consistent with client retry window; duplicate detection metrics are emitted to Console and dashboards.
Runbook and rollback plan exists describing failure modes for multi-region failover with hedged requests and when to disable hedging under overload conditions.
End-to-end integration test harness demonstrates no duplicated committed side-effects for a representative RPC under simulated region outage and heavy traffic.

Canary rollout executed to dedicated tier with telemetry confirming reduced tail latency without increase in duplicate side-effects above an agreed threshold (<=0.1% request duplication for idempotent endpoints).
decisions: Adopt a default client retry window of 10s for interactive text-generation calls and 30s for async/batch endpoints unless overridden by service-level policy.
Server deduplication TTL will be min(client_retry_window + 5s, 60s) to bound storage of idempotency records.

Hedged requests enabled by default for cross-region reads and latency-sensitive generation endpoints with an initial hedge after 120ms of no response, max 1 additional parallel hedge. This is configurable per-route.
Idempotency keys are required for all mutating endpoints; SDKs will auto-generate stable idempotency keys for single-client retries but allow user-supplied keys for multi-client coordination.
Circuit breakers and load-shedding policies are authoritative at the ingress layer: once ingress signals overload, SDKs should back off and avoid client-side hedging to prevent thundering herds.
We will surface duplication and dedupe hit-rate metrics in Console per-model and per-route to enable SLO-aligned tuning.
implementation_plan: Draft spec doc and get alignment with Runtime, API, SDK, and Console leads (1 week).
Prototype server dedupe table and TTL enforcement in runtime; emit dedupe metrics (2 sprints parallel).
Add hedging primitives to gateway/proxy with route-level flags and metrics (1 sprint).
SDK changes: implement default retry windows, idempotency key generation, and hedging control flags across JS/Python/Go (3 sprints, staggered).
Integration tests: simulate region failover, ensure dedupe correctness and measure tail latency improvements (1 sprint).
Canary rollout to Dedicated -> Hosted low-traffic routes, monitor duplication and latency, iterate (2 weeks).
Full rollout and docs + runbook + deprecation guidance for older clients (2 weeks).
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK idempotency key behavior and retry/backoff timers.
Load tests with synthetic traffic to validate ingress load-shedding interaction disables hedging correctly.
Chaos test: force region A to drop and measure client hedged behavior to region B, assert no duplicate side-effects for mutating endpoints in 99.99% of trials.
Long-tail latency tests to quantify hedging benefit and any added cost; measure token-level cost delta and include in acceptance criteria.
Telemetry verification: dedupe hit-rate, duplicate-commit traces, hedged-request counts, and circuit-breaker open events are visible in Console.
rollout_notes: Start with read-heavy routes and non-critical write endpoints in Dedicated to validate operational behavior.
Expose toggles per-customer in Private deployments to opt out of hedging if needed for regulatory reasons.
Prepare a KB article for Solutions and Support describing expected duplication rates and troubleshooting steps.
If duplication exceeds thresholds during canary, immediately disable hedging at ingress and revert SDK hedging flag via remote config.
